sourceCopy.name: Ellipse Calculator
sourceCopy.title: Ellipse Calculator Free | UsefulVerse
sourceCopy.description: Calculate ellipse area, foci, eccentricity and Ramanujan perimeter approximation from two semiaxes. Free and local.
sourceCopy.intro: Enter the two semiaxes of an ellipse to find its area, focal distance, eccentricity and a clearly labeled perimeter approximation.
sourceCopy.howQuestion: What can an ellipse calculator find?
sourceCopy.howAnswer: Given two positive semiaxes, it identifies the major and minor axes, computes area and focus distance, and estimates the perimeter using Ramanujan’s second approximation.
sourceCopy.privacyAnswer: No. The geometry is calculated in this browser. Your values are not sent to a server or stored by this tool.
howTo: Enter the lengths of semiaxes a and b in the same unit.
Calculate to see area, focal distance, eccentricity and perimeter estimate.
Use a consistent area unit (such as cm²) and note the perimeter is approximate.

fields.accuracyNote: Enter positive semiaxis lengths in the same unit, up to 1,000,000,000. Area uses the square of that unit. The perimeter uses Ramanujan’s second approximation, not an exact elementary formula.
fields.formulaNote: Area = πab. Center-to-focus distance c = √(A² − B²), where A is the semi-major axis and B is the semi-minor axis. Eccentricity e = c/A. Perimeter uses Ramanujan II with h = ((A − B)/(A + B))².

messages.copyUnavailable: Copy is unavailable in this browser.
messages.axisRange: Each semiaxis must be positive and no greater than 1,000,000,000.
messages.resultRange: The result exceeds the supported numeric range.

additionalFaqs.question: How do I calculate the area of an ellipse?
additionalFaqs.answer: Multiply π by the semi-major axis and the semi-minor axis. If a and b are the semiaxes, area is πab.

additionalFaqs.question: Is the ellipse perimeter exact?
additionalFaqs.answer: No. There is no simple elementary closed form for a general ellipse perimeter. This tool uses Ramanujan’s second approximation and labels it as approximate.

additionalFaqs.question: What do the foci and eccentricity mean?
additionalFaqs.answer: The two foci lie on the major axis at equal distances from the center. Eccentricity ranges from 0 for a circle toward 1 for increasingly elongated ellipses.
